raw.details:
Project Q – IBM Quantum Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 Hackathon

Build Beyond the Limits. Innovate with Quantum.

Welcome to Project Q, a hybrid quantum computing hackathon organized by SRM University-AP, Amaravati, as part of IBM Quantum Qiskit Fall Fest 2026, an official Partner Plus Host event.

Project Q brings together aspiring developers, students, researchers, and innovators to solve challenging problems using quantum computing and software development. Participate in a competitive, team-based journey that combines online prototyping, technical evaluation, and an intensive 24-hour offline grand finale.

Total Hackathon Prize Pool: ₹1,00,000

About the Hackathon

Project Q is designed to encourage participants to explore practical applications of quantum computing and develop innovative solutions to real-world challenges.

Teams will begin with an online development sprint, selecting a problem statement from one of five specialized domains. After technical evaluation and shortlisting, selected teams will advance to an exciting 24-hour on-campus finale featuring fresh, unreleased problem statements.

Whether you are exploring quantum algorithms, developing optimization solutions, experimenting with quantum machine learning, or investigating quantum-safe cryptography, Project Q offers an opportunity to test your skills and push the boundaries of innovation.

Hackathon Tracks & Problem Statements

Participants can choose from five specialized domains, each offering multiple problem statements and an open innovation option.

1. Quantum Optimization

  • O1: Max-Cut

  • O2: Portfolio Selection

  • O3: Knapsack

  • O-OI: Open Innovation – Custom Optimization Problem

2. Quantum Simulation

  • S1: Ising Chain Ground State

  • S2: Spin Dynamics (Real-Time)

  • S3: Noise in Trotter Simulation

  • S-OI: Open Innovation – Custom Simulation Problem

3. Quantum Machine Learning (QML)

  • Q1: Biomedical Signal Classifier

  • Q2: Quantum Kernel Classifier

  • Q3: Noise-Resilient Classifier

  • Q-OI: Open Innovation – Custom QML Problem

4. Quantum Chemistry

  • C1: Molecular Ground-State Energy (H₂)

  • C2: Diatomic Potential Energy Surface

  • C3: Hardware-Efficient H₂O

  • C-OI: Open Innovation – Custom Chemistry Problem

5. Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC)

  • P1: Quantum-Safe Secure Channel

  • P2: Crypto Inventory & Migration Planner

  • P3: PQC Performance Benchmark

  • P-OI: Open Innovation – Custom PQC Problem

Problem Statements & Deliverables:
Access the Official Problem Statements and Guidelines

Competition Structure

Phase 1: Online – Track Selection & Prototype Sprint

Dates: 8–12 October 2026
Submission Deadline: 12 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST
Format: Online Development Sprint

  • Select a problem statement from one of the five specialized domains.

  • Develop and submit your solution through a GitHub repository.

  • Demonstrate your technical approach, implementation, and performance through a clear report and supporting analysis.

Required Deliverables:

  • One GitHub repository containing an end-to-end implementation (main.ipynb or main.py).

  • A README.md file with setup and execution instructions.

  • Processor definitions and environment files, including requirements.txt, where applicable.

  • A report with supporting figures and graphs, including a comparison of performance, resource usage, and architecture impact.

Phase 2: Online – Technical Code Audit & Rolling Shortlisting

Dates: 12–17 October 2026
Format: Online Technical Evaluation

Submitted repositories will be evaluated based on:

  • Code structure and quality

  • Originality and technical innovation

  • Algorithmic design

  • Reproducibility and implementation

  • Quality of documentation and analysis

Shortlisting announcements will be made on a rolling basis.

Phase 3: Online – Shortlist Verification & Pass Confirmation

Dates: 18–27 October 2026
Format: Virtual Check-in & Confirmation

Only selected teams from the online evaluation rounds will be shortlisted and invited to the 24-hour Grand Finale at SRM University-AP, Amaravati.

  • Shortlisted Teams: Must confirm their participation by purchasing the ₹499 Shortlisted Team Pass per participant on or before 27 October 2026.

  • Non-Shortlisted Applicants: May purchase the ₹499 Open Attendee Pass to visit the campus and participate in parallel events, technical sessions, interactive arenas, and expos, excluding the main hackathon finale.

What Your ₹499 Grand Finale Pass Includes

Your grand finale pass offers more than entry to a hackathon. It gives you an opportunity to experience a leading quantum technology environment and connect with the broader innovation ecosystem.

  • Exclusive Access to India's First Quantum Reference Facility: Get a rare opportunity to explore the Quantum Reference Facility at SRM University-AP and experience India's growing quantum technology ecosystem.

  • Official IBM Quantum Welcome Kit: Receive a branded welcome kit to commemorate your participation in this IBM Quantum event.

  • Complimentary Lunch & Refreshments: Enjoy lunch and two refreshment breaks during the event.

  • 24-Hour Hackathon Experience: Participate in the intensive on-campus grand finale, collaborate with your teammates, and compete for the hackathon prize pool.

  • Quantum Lab Access: Gain access to designated quantum computing laboratory facilities and explore the technical environment supporting quantum research and innovation.

  • Auditorium & Event Venue Access: Attend designated technical sessions, presentations, and event activities at the SRM University-AP campus.

  • Expert Interaction & Networking: Connect with faculty, mentors, fellow innovators, and participants passionate about quantum computing and emerging technologies.

  • Access to Parallel Event Activities: Explore designated exhibitions, interactive arenas, and other activities taking place during Qiskit Fall Fest 2026.

Access to the Quantum Reference Facility, laboratories, and other facilities will be subject to the event schedule, safety protocols, and organizer permissions.

Phase 4: Offline – 24-Hour Grand Finale

Dates: 28 October, 6:00 PM – 29 October, 6:00 PM
Venue: SRM University-AP Campus, Amaravati

The grand finale challenges shortlisted teams to solve a fresh, unreleased problem statement under a 24-hour continuous development sprint.

Key Activities:

  • 28 October, 6:00 PM: Live problem statement reveal, instructions, and commencement of the 24-hour hackathon.

  • 29 October, 10:00 AM: Midway mentor and faculty review checkpoint.

  • 29 October, 4:00–5:00 PM: Circuit benchmarking, live demonstrations, and formal evaluation.

  • 29 October, 6:00 PM: Hacking concludes and final repositories are frozen.

All development for the offline challenge must take place during the designated 24-hour sprint.

Phase 5: Offline – Winner Announcement & Awards

Date: 30 October 2026
Venue: SRM University-AP Campus, Amaravati

The final results and top-performing teams will be announced following the grand finale.

  • Hackathon Prize Pool: ₹1,00,000

  • Trophies and cash prizes for winning teams

  • Certificates and special awards based on jury evaluations

The total prize pool across all Qiskit Fall Fest 2026 events is ₹2,00,000.

Eligibility & Team Formation

  • Open to undergraduate students, postgraduate students, and research scholars.

  • Teams must consist of 2–6 members.

  • Inter-institutional teams are permitted.

  • All team members must be registered under this opportunity before the Phase 1 submission deadline.

Tools & Technology

Participants can use standard quantum software frameworks, including Qiskit, along with the specified hardware backends and simulators.

Submissions must include the complete source code, execution instructions, dependency lists, test runs, and technical documentation required for evaluation.

Rules & Guidelines

Originality & Academic Integrity

  • All submitted work must be original.

  • Plagiarism, repository scraping, or misattribution will result in immediate team disqualification.

  • Generative AI tools are permitted only for syntax support, documentation, and troubleshooting. Circuit architecture and core algorithms must be implemented by the team.

  • Decisions of the judging committee and organizing panel are final.

Online and Offline Development

  • Phase 1 solutions must address the published online problem statements to qualify for shortlisting.

  • The offline grand finale will feature new, unreleased problem statements.

  • Code developed before the offline problem statement is revealed will not be accepted as part of the offline challenge.

Why Participate?

  • Solve Real-World Challenges: Work on problems across quantum optimization, simulation, machine learning, chemistry, and cryptography.

  • Showcase Your Skills: Demonstrate your technical abilities through a competitive, multi-phase hackathon.

  • Experience a 24-Hour Finale: Challenge yourself in an intensive, on-campus development sprint.

  • Explore India's Quantum Ecosystem: Get an opportunity to visit India's first Quantum Reference Facility at SRM University-AP, subject to the event schedule and access permissions.

  • Connect with Innovators: Engage with fellow participants, mentors, faculty, and the broader quantum technology community.

  • Compete for ₹1,00,000: Earn recognition and awards for your innovation and technical excellence.

Take on the challenge. Build innovative solutions. Experience quantum innovation up close. Be part of Project Q at IBM Quantum Qiskit Fall Fest 2026.
